slides.heading: Optimal Freelancing
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Greedy Algorithms
slides.narration: Let's solve Optimal Freelancing, an easy greedy algorithms problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Each job takes one day and has a deadline (days left) and a payment.
Working at most 7 days, one job per day, maximise profit.
Greedy: take jobs by payment descending and place each in the latest free day on or before its deadline.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Each job takes one day and has a deadline (days left) and a payment. Working at most 7 days, one job per day, maximise profit. Greedy: take jobs by payment descending and place each in the latest free day on or before its deadline.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Greedy by payment: take the most valuable jobs first and schedule each as late as its deadline allows.
slides.narration: Greedy by payment: take the most valuable jobs first and schedule each as late as its deadline allows.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Sort jobs by payment, highest first
3. Place each job in the latest free day before its deadline
4. Sum the payments of placed jobs
slides.narration: Step by step. First, sort jobs by payment, highest first. Second, keep seven day slots. Third, place each job in the latest free day before its deadline. Fourth, sum the payments of placed jobs.
